ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or answer questions. But, you know what? Even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't know the secret formula, hajimete no koto (the first time).

These networks are made up of many layers, like a big stack of pancakes, tori tori (flap flap). Each layer is trying to solve a problem, but they're not always sure how, kono mono wa nan desu ka? (what is this thing). So, even the creators can't explain everything, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind).

It's not that they're not smart, it's just that these networks are really, really complex, nan desu ka? (what is this?). They're like a big, messy puzzle, and even the creators can't solve it, hajimete no koto (the first time).

But, that's okay! The creators are still really good at making these networks work, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?). They just need to keep experimenting and learning, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). And who knows, maybe one day they'll figure out the secret formula, hajimete no koto (the first time)!
